overview: The MPS School Committee oversees the Medford Public Schools, managing district policy, budgeting, and facility planning. Over the five-year span from late 2021 to 2026, the body transitioned from pandemic-era health protocols to a primary focus on large-scale infrastructure projects and long-term academic stability. Key initiatives include the comprehensive renovation or replacement of Medford High School through the MSBA process and addressing severe elementary school overcrowding. The committee also navigated significant leadership changes, including the departure of Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent and the subsequent appointment of Dr. Suzanne Galusi. As of the most recent records, the committee is finalizing technical HVAC selections for elementary schools and monitoring the feasibility phase of the high school building project.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a formal stakeholder committee in early 2022 to define the vision for a new or renovated high school. Following acceptance into the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) core program, the body established a formal building committee and selected an Owner's Project Manager to lead the feasibility study. The project encountered challenges in 2026 after a 999-year DCR deed restriction on Edgley Field forced the elimination of several design options. Current work involves evaluating six remaining alternatives, including both new construction and addition-renovation models, ahead of a scheduled local authorization vote in 2027.

threads.name: Elementary School Capacity and Redistricting
threads.summary: Enrollment pressures were first identified at the McGlynn school in 2021, eventually escalating into a capacity crisis at Roberts Elementary where enrollment surpassed 590 students. To address overcrowding, the committee relocated preschool classrooms to the Missituk and authorized several space utilization studies. Members have debated school restructuring models, such as moving to a K-4 and 5-8 grade configuration, while attempting to formalize a district-wide elementary reassignment policy. Recent actions include the creation of a task force to review facilities utilization and planning for potential redistricting for the 2027-2028 school year.

threads.name: Labor Relations and Collective Bargaining
threads.summary: The committee managed complex negotiations starting with COVID-era testing and vaccination protocols for staff in 2021. Contract talks with the Medford Teachers Association reached a formal impasse in late 2022 before resulting in a ratified four-year agreement that adjusted the elementary school schedule. Successive agreements were reached for paraprofessionals, custodians, and secretaries through 2024. In 2025, the committee ratified a new three-year teachers' contract that added fifteen minutes to the school day and reduced half-day releases.

threads.name: High School Safety and Climate
threads.summary: Following reports of student insecurity and a violent bathroom stabbing in 2022, the committee implemented a 10-point safety plan involving bathroom occupancy limits and hallway monitoring. An independent assessment by consultant Michael Welch recommended leadership transitions and unified scheduling to improve the school's culture. The committee subsequently authorized capital expenditures for vape detectors, security cameras, and cleaning equipment to improve bathroom conditions. In 2026, the body introduced a late-bus service to expand access to after-school activities for students with transportation barriers.

threads.name: Infrastructure and HVAC Modernization
threads.summary: The district has pursued an aggressive capital plan to address failing HVAC systems and obsolete refrigerants at the McGlynn, Andrews, and Roberts schools. The committee approved a $25 million bond for comprehensive replacements at the middle schools and successfully applied for MSBA Accelerated Repair grants for multiple elementary facilities. Environmental considerations led the body to prohibit the purchase of new fossil-fuel equipment without authorization and select geothermal heat pump systems for the Missituk and Roberts projects. Testing for lead in water fixtures also resulted in the installation of filtered bottle-filling stations district-wide.

threads.name: Literacy and Academic Assessment
threads.summary: The district transitioned its elementary literacy instruction to align with the 'science of reading,' moving away from three-cueing models. After a multi-year review, the committee approved the adoption of Houghton Mifflin Harcourt's 'Into Reading' as the core elementary curriculum. The body utilizes NWEA MAP testing to monitor student growth and identify learning gaps exacerbated by the pandemic. Recent work has focused on implementing honors pilots for vocational students and revising graduation requirements to replace the state MCAS mandate with successful completion of aligned coursework.

threads.name: Before and After School Programming
threads.summary: Initially plagued by long waitlists and staffing shortages, the before and after school programs underwent significant structural changes including the implementation of a lottery system for kindergartners. The committee partnered with the BASIC collaborative to expand capacity, eventually adding over 150 seats and transitioning to a model with full-time site directors. Tuition rates were adjusted to a sliding-scale model to ensure accessibility for economically disadvantaged families. By late 2026, the district reported a 50 percent increase in enrollment and a substantial reduction in waitlisted students.
